stories.title: BMC approves 15-year Raymond deal for helipad at Coastal Road South jetty
stories.summary: The BMC Standing Committee on Thursday approved a proposal seeking appointment of Raymond Ltd as the developer and operator of a helipad planned to come up at an existing jetty site at the Coastal Road South. Congress on Friday opposed the appointment, demanding that water metro should be built at the jetty instead, claiming that this would be a more beneficial mode of public transport.

stories.title: Mumbai: Two golden jackals killed at same spot on Airoli-Mulund Link Road
stories.summary: A golden jackal was killed in a road accident on the Airoli-Mulund Link Road on Friday, November 27, raising fresh concerns over recurring wildlife deaths on the busy stretch. The high-speed road cuts through a natural mangrove corridor connecting the Airoli-Bhandup wetlands, and naturalists fear animals attempting to cross it are falling victim to speeding vehicles.

stories.title: Maharashtra govt clears Navi Mumbai’s final DP
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government has cleared the remaining excluded portions of Navi Mumbai’s Development Plan (DP), approving changes to land-use designations, reservations, roads and civic amenities across seven nodes. The November 23 notification completes the state’s approval process for the plan, retaining the Advali-Bhutvali green belt but dropping proposed cycle tracks.

stories.title: Two arrested with charas worth ₹12.20 crore at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai
stories.summary: 20 crore from their possession at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) during an operation conducted on the intervening night of November 24 and 25. A case was registered on November 25 under Sections 8(c), 20(c) and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

stories.title: Mumbai: Fire breaks out in Kandivali East residential building
stories.summary: A Level-I fire broke out on the fourth floor of a residential building in Kandivali East, Mumbai, on Friday, November 27. The fire was extinguished by the Mumbai Fire Brigade, and no injuries were reported in the incident. As per the officials, the fire was reported at around 8:50 pm on November 27 at Saraswati Building, located in Thakur Village near D-Mart, Kandivali East.

stories.title: Mumbai architects urge wetland park at Mahalaxmi Racecourse
stories.summary: The Mumbai Architects Collective (MAC), comprising architects, urbanists and transport experts, has written to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, welcoming the decision to drop the proposed underground sports complex, convention facility and multilevel car park at Mahalaxmi Racecourse. The collective has sought a formal written order confirming the decision and urged the state government to introduce a permanent policy protecting the city’s public open spaces.

stories.title: 17-yr-old dies after dogs chase him in Badlapur
stories.summary: A 17-year-old Class 12 student died after a pack of stray dogs allegedly chased him in Badlapur West on Thursday. The teenager, who had undergone bypass surgery three years ago, ran to escape the dogs and soon developed chest discomfort and breathing difficulties. He was rushed to Badlapur Rural Hospital, where he was declared dead.

stories.title: Congress opposes proposal to hand over Worli jetty to private firm for helipad, seeks Water Metro terminal
stories.summary: The Congress has opposed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) proposal to hand over the Worli jetty to a private company for constructing a helipad, arguing that the site should instead be developed as a Water Metro terminal to promote public transport. The proposal was passed at the standing committee meeting on Thursday.

stories.title: NCP(SP) poised to break Opposition ranks, Supriya Sule likely to skip INDIA bloc meet over delimitation bill
stories.summary: As the Union Cabinet cleared the delimitation bill to restructure the country’s parliamentary constituencies on Friday, it was clear that the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) is likely to break ranks with the Congress to support the bill, if only to stall defection of its MPs, said party insiders.

stories.title: Commuter attacked with sharp weapon after confronting beedi smokers
stories.summary: A passenger was allegedly slashed in the face with a sharp weapon after he objected to two men smoking beedis inside the luggage compartment of a moving Kasara-CSMT slow local on Friday morning. The attack, which took place between Kalyan and Thakurli, left the commuter injured near his eye.

stories.title: Mumbai: Two forest guards arrested for molesting minor girls at SGNP
stories.summary: Two forest guards posted with the Revenue and Forest Department in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, formerly Aurangabad, have been arrested by Kasturba Marg police for allegedly molesting two minor girls who had visited Sanjay Gandhi National Park for an outing. 30 pm on November 26, when the two girls, residents of Mumbai, were walking near a lake close to the toy train station.

stories.title: 4 armed robbers smash car windows, escape with 16.4kg gold worth Rs 20 crore in daring Navi Mumbai heist
stories.summary: Four men armed with iron rods robbed 16 kg and 400 grams of gold bars worth around Rs 20 crore after intercepting a car carrying the bullion and occupied by four employees of a jewellery manufacturing unit located in Nerul MIDC. 54pm, when they reached the service road near Juinagar railway station, a WagonR car approached from the opposite direction and intercepted their vehicle.

stories.title: 60-year-old woman sexually assaulted inside Mumbai's Ghatkopar railway station washroom; 25-year-old arrested
stories.summary: A 60-year-old woman was sexually assaulted and hit on her forehead inside a public washroom at Ghatkopar railway station late on Thursday. The woman lives in Khadavli and comes to Ghatkopar, where she works as a daily wager. After finishing her work, she and her daughter went to Ghatkopar railway station to take a train to Khadavli.

stories.title: Mumbai: BMC Completes 23 Leak Repairs On Key Water Pipelines Between Powai Reservoir And Sahar Within 24-Hour
stories.summary: The civic body repaired 14 leakages in the 1,800 mm and 2,400 mm pipelines by deploying teams inside the pipelines, as external repairs were not technically feasible. Another nine leakages in the 600 mm pipeline were also successfully plugged. A team of 20 engineers and 180 workers from the Hydraulic Engineer's Department worked round the clock to complete the operation.

stories.title: Gig war: A slugfest between riders and platforms
stories.summary: Since November last year, delivery and ride-hailing platforms have owed up to 2% of their turnover to a fund for riders on platforms such as Zomato and Swiggy among others. Last week, the government made public a proposal it is considering: why not charge it on every order instead?

stories.title: Bandra railway station celebrates 162 years with three-day festival
stories.summary: Mumbai’s iconic Bandra railway station is celebrating its 162nd anniversary with a three-day heritage and cultural festival, bringing together history, art, music and public participation at one of the city's finest railway landmarks. Organised by Western Railway’s Mumbai Division, the Bandra Station Mahotsav 2026 is being held from November 27 to 29 to commemorate the station’s opening on November 28, 1864.

stories.title: WR successfully tests Kavach safety system on Virar-Mumbai Central route
stories.summary: It could sound like a sequence straight out of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) — a locomotive approaching a red signal, a simulated collision scenario, and an electronic system intervening to avert danger. Except this was no video game. Over two nights, November 20-21 and 21-22, Western Railway (WR) engineers were testing India’s indigenous train protection system, Kavach, along the 50-km Virar-Mumbai Central suburban railway corridor.

stories.title: Mumbai BEST workers protest, threaten strike from Dec 21
stories.summary: The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) workers' union has threatened an indefinite strike from December 21 if its demands are not met, an official statement said on Friday. The union will conduct a ballot on December 4 to seek the opinion of permanent and waitlisted employees on whether to go ahead with the proposed strike.

stories.title: Two held for molesting minor girls at Sanjay Gandhi National Park
stories.summary: Two forest guards were arrested for allegedly molesting two minor girls at Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) on Thursday. The girls called the police helpline after the men allegedly followed them near a lake, asked for their phone numbers and touched them inappropriately. The accused, Umesh Markande and Prabhu Chormare, both around 35, had reportedly travelled from Aurangabad to Mumbai as tourists.

stories.title: 500+ cops to be deployed at Diljit Dosanjh's Mumbai concert following bomb threat email
stories.summary: More than 500 Mumbai police personnel will be deployed at Mahalaxmi Racecourse here for actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert on Friday following a threat email warning of possible attacks on the venue and Metro stations, officials said. Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) teams have swept the venue, they said, adding that entry checks will be carried out across all five gates instead of three.

stories.title: Mumbai curator's sun artwork installed at UN headquarters in Geneva
stories.summary: India, literally, has its moment in the sun as a sun artwork/installation conceptualised and curated by Mumbai’s Jalpa H Vithalani and created by artist Professor Dr UdayRaj Gadnis, has been installed in the Meditation Room at the Palais des Nations, United Nations (UN) in Geneva, Switzerland. The inauguration took place on November 17.

stories.title: Parel railway land residents await High Court relief as demolition fears persist
stories.summary: With no official stay order in place and the petition yet to be submitted before the Bombay High Court , those residing on railway land at the southern end of Prabhadevi station in Parel continue to live with uncertainty over the fate of their homes. stories.title: Thane traffic alert: Restrictions across Kasarvadavli, Kapurbawdi and Wagle
stories.summary: The Thane Traffic Division has announced traffic restrictions across parts of the city on Sunday, November 29, in view of the Lokmat Marathon 2026. 30 am across the Kasarvadavli, Kapurbawdi and Wagle traffic sub-divisions. stories.title: Mumbai’s first anti-conversion case turns newly-weds’ lives upside down
stories.summary: Instead of honeymooning in Kashmir as they had originally planned, a newly-wed couple in Mumbai’s Jogeshwari (East) is starting their married life fearfully confined in their tiny home in a congested by-lane. Mohammad Faiz Akbar Khan, 26, who runs a food cart in the neighbourhood married Shravani Rane, 22, on October 16 under the Special Marriage Act.

Victory to Lord Murugan! Victory to Lord Murugan!”

stories.summary: Two people were killed and three others injured after the vehicle they were travelling in veered off the road and plunged into a gorge in Himachal Pradesh’s Sundernagar in Mandi district, police said on Friday. The accident occurred near the Pandar police outpost in the Nihri area of Sundernagar when the vehicle, carrying five people, was returning from a wedding ceremony.

stories.title: Man dies by suicide at his mother’s home in Faridabad | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: A 19-year-old man died by suicide at his mother’s home in Bhupani on Wednesday, police said on Friday, adding that an inquiry had been conducted into the circumstances surrounding his death. The deceased lived with his uncle in Delhi’s Shalimar Bagh and had recently come to stay with his mother ahead of his 20th birthday on Saturday.

stories.title: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
stories.summary: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the territorial government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

stories.title: Truck driver killed as vehicle crashes into NH-9 barrier near Dasna | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man was killed after his truck hit the side barrier of the National Highway-9 (NH-9) near Dasna on Friday, police said, adding that he allegedly lost control of his truck. 15 when the truck, loaded with hay sacks, was headed to Chappraula in Gautam Budh Nagar, police said.

stories.title: Guindy Children’s Park shuts down after 14 birds die of avian flu
stories.summary: The children’s park in Guindy will remain closed for three days from Saturday (Nov 28) or until further orders after 14 waterbirds died in their enclosure on Friday. Chennai wildlife warden K Bharagava Teja confirmed that four painted storks and 10 night herons had died, and samples have been sent to National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal to check for Avian flu.

stories.title: ‘If India is strong, Sanatan Dharma will be strong’: UP CM Yogi Adityanath
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday described India and 'Sanatan Dharma' as complementary to each other, asserting that guided by this ethos, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Nation First' mantra should become the guiding resolve of every Indian. stories.title: Delimitation Bill proposes formation of commission, SC judge, CEC nominee among members
stories.summary: A delimitation commission will be immediately constituted after The Delimitation (Second) Bill takes effect, according to a copy of the document accessed by HT. According to the document, the proposed three-member delimitation commission will include a serving or former Supreme Court judge, the Chief Election Commissioner or one of the Election Commissioners (ex-officio) appointed by him and a state election commissioner.

stories.summary: “Our large dependence on imports has shown that we are so vulnerable that we may be caught in a tight situation and it can be disastrous for the country. High prices of crude and natural gas are costing us at least Rs 6-7 lakh crore extra every year.

stories.title: Ludhiana: Parking dispute escalates into acid attack; 2 injured | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: A minor dispute over parking a vehicle escalated into an acid attack in the Tibba area, where the owner of a metal scrap unit and his accomplices attacked two brothers with baseball bats before throwing acid on one of them, leaving him severely burnt.

stories.title: Groom’s sister shot dead during celebratory firing at Bahadurgarh wedding | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: A 30-year-old woman was shot dead during celebratory firing at her brother’s wedding in Jhajjar’s Bahadurgarh on Thursday night, police said on Friday, adding that the suspect, a close friend of the groom, was absconding. The deceased, Manisha, a resident of Rewari, had come to her parental home with her husband, Khushi Ram, and their two children to attend her brother Amandeep’s wedding.

stories.title: El Nino-linked deluges flood cities in Peru, Ecuador | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: Several cities in Peru and Ecuador faced major flooding on Friday after downpours in the region linked to the exceptionally strong El Nino phenomenon. In Piura, capital of the eponymous region in northern Peru, waist-high water filled city streets following 12 hours of heavy rains that began on Thursday.

stories.title: ‘One community favoured’: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President, alleges bias in collegium picks
stories.summary: Former Chief Justice of India Bhushan R Gavai has written to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that the Supreme Court collegium is increasingly favouring candidates from “one particular section of the society” for elevation to constitutional courts, to the exclusion of scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women.

stories.summary: An employee at a hotel in Meerut was arrested after a video, purportedly showing him spitting on a roti during food preparation, went viral on social media, police said on Friday. stories.summary: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought.

stories.summary: Rohit Sharma will return as Mumbai Indians captain for the 2027 Indian Premier League (IPL) season, the franchise announced on Friday. The announcement comes following Hardik Pandya's trade to Punjab Kings (PBKS) ahead of the IPL 2027 auction next month. Hardik had replaced Rohit as Mumbai Indians captain ahead of the 2024 season, following his return to the franchise from Gujarat Titans.

stories.title: World chess championship: Sindarov admits Gukesh out-prepared him in third game
stories.summary: Challenger Javokhir Sindarov admitted he was out-prepared by defending champion D Gukesh in the third game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva, as the Indian's opening preparation put the Uzbek under pressure. 5 after three consecutive draws, Sindarov acknowledged that Gukesh, who was playing with Black pieces in Game 3, had caught him off guard with his preparation in the opening.

stories.title: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy: Azharuddeen’s century powers Kerala into the Super League
stories.summary: Mohammed Azharuddeen’s signature rocking-the-bat celebration has become a defining moment in this season’s Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 cricket tournament. The opening batter brought it out once again on Friday for his second T20 hundred (101, 57b, 8x4, 6x6) which dismantled Himachal Pradesh and helped Kerala register a 67-run win to qualify for the Super League.

stories.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
stories.summary: Manchester United reporter Published 4 minutes ago Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract. The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources with an understanding of the situation say both parties decided it was in their best interests to trigger the option.

stories.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal overtakes Virat Kohli for unwanted WTC record
stories.summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal endured a disappointing outing with the bat, falling for a six-ball duck on Day 2 of the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. Jaiswal has now registered eight ducks in WTC matches, going past Virat Kohli, who has been dismissed for zero seven times.

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers seemingly hits back at Tom Brady over accusation of violating locker room sanctity
stories.summary: The saga of Aaron Rodgers' controversial departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers continued Friday, even as the team recorded a win in their first game since Rodgers left. Rodgers on Friday seemingly responded to Tom Brady , who accused the former Steelers quarterback of violating dressing-room sanctity by going public about his fallout with Steelers management.

stories.title: Rohit Sharma's return as captain doesn't guarantee success for MI in IPL 2027: Ashwin
stories.summary: Rohit has reclaimed the leadership role after three seasons away from it , taking over from Hardik Pandya, who has moved to Punjab Kings in a trade involving Arshdeep Singh. The decision marks another change in Mumbai's leadership structure as the franchise looks to rediscover the success it enjoyed under Rohit.

stories.title: Women’s Asian Champions Trophy Final: Inexperienced China has its task cut out against hat-trick seeking India
stories.summary: A rampaging India will aim for a hat-trick of Asian Champions Trophy titles when it takes on China in the gold medal clash here at the International Sports Complex on Saturday. India has won six in six matches and is enjoying a 14-game winning run. It took down Malaysia once again in the semifinal with a 6-2 scoreline.

stories.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
stories.summary: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations.

stories.title: Fury cleared to fight Joshua after wife retracts schizophrenia claim
stories.summary: Tyson Fury has been medically cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in December after the bout was put in jeopardy by claims of a schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury, 38, spoke of his mental health struggles in a Netflix documentary which was released on Friday, with his wife, Paris, saying he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia.

stories.title: 'He will win games single-handedly': Ex-cricketer backs Sooryavanshi for ODI World Cup
stories.summary: Impressed by the youngster's fearless approach, Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi has the potential to become an all-format cricketer and should not be restricted to a particular format. Kris Srikkanth backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World CupSrikkanth believes Sooryavanshi deserves to be included in India's 15-member squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, even if the team management is not yet convinced about his readiness for Test cricket.

stories.title: Could Rohit Sharma’s Return As MI Captain Force Jasprit Bumrah To Leave Mumbai Indians?
stories.summary: Mumbai Indians' leadership decisions could have an impact on Jasprit Bumrah's future with the franchise ahead of the IPL 2028 mega auction. The star Indian fast bowler was reportedly approached by the franchise's top management for the role of vice-captain before Rohit Sharma was identified as the preferred choice to lead the team.

stories.title: Jasprit Bumrah's 274-ball wicket drought tests India's faith in 'Jassi bhai'
stories.summary: Jasprit Bumrah beat the bat on numerous occasions, found edges that didn't carry, and kept kicking the turf in frustration, but remained wicketless. His 274-ball drought was the second-longest he has gone without picking up a wicket in Test cricket. It's Bumrah. He isn't meant to wait.

stories.title: Why the Supreme Court wants red warning labels on unhealthy packaged foods | Explained
stories.summary: Packaged food products high in sugar, saturated fat or salt could soon carry prominent red warning labels on the front of their packs, alerting consumers to their nutritional content. The Supreme Court, earlier this week, directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) regime and gave the regulator four months to finalise the draft regulations.

stories.title: What we know about Department for Work and Pensions 'cyber incident'
stories.summary: While the DWP has said benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal, the department is continuing to investigate the cause of the incident. Nearly all of the DWP's online systems have been taken down, including those for pensions, universal credit and Pip applications, as well as the "Tell Us Once'" system used to let the government know if someone has died.

stories.title: Do Indian bodies burn calories differently? Country’s 1st advanced metabolic chamber seeks answers
stories.summary: The Human Metabolic Chamber at Vellore’s Christian Medical College (CMC) was jointly established by the college and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research’s (TIFR) Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) and is designed to give researchers a more precise picture of how the human body burns calories and uses different sources of energy.

stories.title: Spain’s 2026 election explained in maps and charts
stories.summary: google Add Al Jazeera on Spain will hold a snap election on November 29 that could bring the far right into government for the first time since the end of Francisco Franco’s dictatorship in 1975.

stories.title: Why is COP31 perceived to be a failure? | Explained
stories.summary: The immediate trigger was a “cover text” put forward by COP 31 president Murat Kurum, Turkiye’s Environment Minister. This is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a conference and is usually finalised last. Like every outcome, it needs the agreement of all parties. No country or bloc holds a veto but every clause must be accepted by all 190-plus delegations.

stories.title: Mint explainer: why HPV vaccination is critical for girls as India crosses 10 million doses
stories.summary: India has administered more than 10 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months under a campaign by the Union health ministry. The drive has covered nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 12 million girls, drawing praise from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) South-East Asia Region.

stories.title: Why does your Wi-Fi work even when radio signals bounce off walls?
stories.summary: The evolution of Wi-Fi technology is a fascinating tale of global collaboration. It began with Hedy Lamarr and George Antheil's innovative frequency-hopping idea during World War II. Subsequent advancements were made by CSIRO researchers in Australia, who enhanced indoor wireless communication. S. played a crucial role by opening up radio frequencies for unlicensed use, setting standards that paved the way for the wireless networks we rely on today.

stories.title: Netanyahu may offer rival rotating PM deal amid coalition uncertainty; will Eisenkot accept? | Explained
stories.summary: Weeks after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the country's election to his rival, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, the former is reportedly preparing to offer his rival the position of prime minister in a rotational government, local media reported. According to The Times of Israel , Netanyahu is willing to serve as the second prime minister.

stories.title: Explained: What's Behind Delay In Delhi Winter And When To Expect Cold Wave
stories.summary: Climate experts and meteorologists say that while a hint of the cold may be in, a sustained cold wave is still at least two weeks away kept at bay by a lack of active Western Disturbances, urban heat trapping, and a strong El Nino event unfolding in the Pacific.

stories.title: What is the Indraprastha Communique issued after SCO Civilizational Forum in New Delhi? | Explained
stories.summary: India hosted the first “Civilisational Dialogue Forum” of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) grouping, that includes Pakistan, from November 20-22 at Delhi’s historic Purana Qila. The dialogue, which was organized by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council.

stories.title: Is Iraq facing renewed instability?
stories.summary: The local government runs the oil fields and revenue helps it govern. But now that is in danger. The federal government has announced control over refineries. Baghdad says it’s losing millions of dollars every month to crude oil smugglers. That’s united the Kurds who are bitterly opposed to the move.
